2609.21748.title: World Modeling in Transformers
2609.21748.paper_summary: Behavioral failures can make a transformer appear to lack a world model even when it has learned faithful representations of its environment. We demonstrate this in TaxiGPT, a transformer trained on random walks through Manhattan whose failures have been interpreted as evidence of an incoherent internal map. Through mechanistic analysis and causal interventions, we show that the model represents intersections and streets, tracks its position, and uses a goal compass to navigate. We trace its failures to interference between superposed intersection features, which disrupts localization within the internal map. Affordance packing, which groups representations of intersections with the same legal moves, helps limit the consequences of these errors. Finally, we propose mechanistic indicators that we use to compare models and show that world-modeling capacities emerge at different stages of training. Our findings motivate a shift from asking whether a model has a world model to mechanistically studying its world modeling: the interacting capacities through which it represents its environment and uses those representations to guide behavior.
2609.21748.paper_summary_zh: 行為失敗可能使Transformer看起來缺乏世界模型，即使它已經學會了對其環境的忠實表徵。我們在TaxiGPT中展示了這一點，這是一個在曼哈頓隨機行走訓練的Transformer，其失敗被解釋為內部地圖不連貫的證據。通過機械分析和因果干預，我們展示了該模型如何表示交叉口和街道，追蹤其位置，並使用目標羅盤進行導航。我們將其失敗追溯到重疊交叉口特徵之間的干擾，這會干擾內部地圖中的定位。可供性打包將具有相同合法移動的交叉口表徵進行分組，有助於限制這些錯誤的後果。最後，我們提出了機械指標，用於比較模型，並顯示世界建模能力在訓練的不同階段出現。我們的發現促使我們從詢問模型是否具有世界模型轉向機械性地研究其世界建模：通過與環境互動的能力，利用這些表徵來指導行為。
